events.n: Writing begins in Sumer and Egypt
events.t: Cuneiform and hieroglyphs are first used in the late fourth millennium BC, at Uruk and in the Nile valley.
About 3100 BC the Nile valley comes under one court; the First Dynasty begins.
The mature Harappan phase begins about 2600 BC; the Indus civilisation ends about 1700 BC.
Sargon unites the cities of Sumer and Akkad and marches to the Mediterranean; the empire is founded in the late twenty-fourth century BC.
src: Wikipedia, List of people known as the Great

events.t: The oldest record of Hammurabi's law code dates to about 1780 BC.
The Minoan eruption buries Akrotiri about 1600 BC.
The Shang rule the Yellow River plain from about 1600 BC until the Zhou overthrow the last Shang king about 1046 BC.
Between about 1200 and 1150 BC the palace states of Greece, Anatolia and the Levant fall and the trade of the eastern Mediterranean breaks down.
About 1046 BC the Zhou defeat the last Shang king and rule from the Wei valley.
Phoenicians from Tyre found Carthage in 814 BC.
The first recorded games are held at Olympia in 776 BC.
Rome is founded in 753 BC by the traditional reckoning.
Babylonians, Medes and Scythians destroy Nineveh in 612 BC and the Assyrian empire ends.

events.n: The Buddha teaches in the Ganges plain
events.t: Siddhartha Gautama, born about 563 BC by the traditional count, teaches in the Ganges plain and dies about 483 BC.
Cyrus the Great takes Babylon in 539 BC, ends the Neo-Babylonian empire and frees the Jewish exiles.
Tarquin the Proud is expelled and the Republic founded in 509 BC.
The Greek cities defeat the Persian landing at Marathon in 490 BC.
Xerxes crosses the Hellespont in 480 BC, forces Thermopylae and burns Athens, but his fleet is beaten at Salamis.
Athens and Sparta fight from 431 to 404 BC; Athens loses.
Alexander crosses to Asia in 334 BC, wins at the Granicus, Issus and Gaugamela, takes Egypt, Persia and Bactria, turns back at the Hyphasis in 326 and dies in Babylon in June 323 BC.
src: Wikipedia, Chronology of the expedition of Alexander the Great into Asia

events.t: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the Nanda dynasty of Magadha in 321 BC.
Ashoka conquers Kalinga in 261 BC and afterwards sends Buddhist missions abroad, to Sri Lanka among others.
Qin Shi Huang conquers the other warring states and takes the title of emperor in 221 BC.
Hannibal leaves New Carthage in 218 BC, crosses the Rhône and the Alps with fewer than 35,000 men left, wins in Italy and is beaten by Scipio at Zama in 202 BC.
src: Wikipedia, Hannibal's crossing of the Alps

events.t: The Han are established in 206 BC; trade links with the West open along what becomes the Silk Road.
The Third Punic War ends with the destruction of Carthage in 146 BC.

Caesar beats the Helvetii at Bibracte in 58 BC and the Belgae at the Sabis in 57, destroys the Veneti fleet in 56, bridges the Rhine and lands in Britain in 55 and 54, and takes Vercingetorix at Alesia in 52 BC.
Caesar crosses the Rubicon in January 49 BC, rules as dictator and is murdered on 15 March 44 BC.
Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra off Actium in 31 BC.
Octavian receives the title Augustus in 27 BC and rules until his death in AD 14.

events.n: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
events.t: Arminius destroys three Roman legions in AD 9.
Jesus is crucified at Jerusalem between AD 30 and 33; the exact year is unknown.
Paul's journeys of about 45–57 carry the new faith from Antioch through Cyprus and Anatolia to Macedonia, Athens, Corinth and Ephesus.
Buddhism comes to China in 67 with the monks Kasyapa and Dharmaraksha; the White Horse Temple is founded at Luoyang in 68.
Titus's armies destroy Jerusalem and its Temple in AD 70.
Vesuvius destroys Pompeii in AD 79.
Under Trajan, from the conquest of Dacia to 117, the Roman Empire reaches its largest extent.
Work on Hadrian's Wall begins in 122.
The Han dynasty falls in 220 and the Three Kingdoms period begins.
Armenia becomes the first kingdom to make Christianity its state religion, in 301.
Constantine and Licinius grant toleration to Christians in 313.
The first ecumenical council meets at Nicaea in 325.
The kingdom of Aksum declares Christianity its state religion under King Ezana; the timeline dates it to 325.
Constantine names his new capital on the Bosporus in 330.
The Goths destroy the eastern army and kill the emperor Valens in 378.
Theodosius makes Nicene Christianity the religion of the empire in 380.
Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome in 410.
St Patrick begins his mission in Ireland in 432.

events.n: The end of the Western Empire
events.t: Odoacer forces Romulus Augustulus to abdicate in 476.
Clovis, king of the Franks, is baptised at Reims in 496.
Belisarius retakes North Africa from the Vandals in 533; the Gothic War of 535–554 brings Italy back under Constantinople at great cost.

events.t: Plague carried on grain ships from Egypt reaches Constantinople in 541–542 and kills perhaps two-fifths of the city; waves recur until about 750.

events.t: Magellan's fleet leaves Seville on 10 August 1519 and passes the strait on 28 November 1520; Magellan is killed at Mactan in 1521 and Elcano brings the Victoria home on 6 September 1522.
Suleiman defeats and kills Louis II of Hungary at Mohács in 1526.
Suleiman's army reaches Vienna on 27 September 1529 and abandons the siege on 14 October.
The Spanish conquest of the Inca empire begins in 1532 and the Inca capital is in Spanish hands within a year.
Copernicus's heliocentric treatise appears in 1543, the year he dies at Frombork.
The council that shapes the Catholic Counter-Reformation sits at Trent from 1545 to 1563.
Kazan falls to Ivan IV after a siege in 1552 and Astrakhan is annexed in 1556; the Volga is Russian to the Caspian.
From 1565 galleons link Manila and Acapulco, once Urdaneta finds the eastward route.
The Holy League's galleys defeat the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto in 1571.

The Armada sails on 28 May 1588, fights its way up the Channel, is scattered by fireships at Calais, beaten at Gravelines on 8 August and returns round Scotland and Ireland with heavy losses to storms.
The Dutch trading companies merge into the VOC in 1602.
Tokugawa Ieyasu takes the title of shogun in 1603 and rules from Edo.
The English settle Jamestown in Virginia in 1607.
Galileo observes the moons of Jupiter in 1610.
Thirty years of war across the Empire, from Prague in 1618 to the Peace of Westphalia in 1648; the French beat Spain's tercios at Rocroi in 1643.
The Mayflower sails from Plymouth to New England in 1620.
Galileo stands trial before the Inquisition in Rome in 1633.
The Manchu conquest ends the Ming in 1644; the Qing rule from Beijing.
The peace of 1648 ends the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War.
Charles I is executed for high treason in 1649, after the civil war that began in 1642.
The Ottoman army besieges Vienna in 1683; the Holy League relieves the city, and the Great Turkish War ends at Karlowitz in 1699 with Hungary ceded to the Habsburgs.
Newton publishes the Principia in 1687.
William of Orange lands in England in 1688; the settlement of 1689 makes England a constitutional monarchy.
Peter travels incognito from March 1697 through Riga and Königsberg to Zaandam and Amsterdam, reaches London in January 1698, visits Vienna and hurries home on news of the Streltsy rising.
Peter founds Saint Petersburg on Hare Island in the Neva on 29 June 1703.
Peter's army defeats Charles XII of Sweden at Poltava on 27 June 1709.
The treaty of 1721 ends the Great Northern War; Russia gains Ingria, Estonia and Livonia and Peter is proclaimed emperor.
Nader Shah of Persia invades and plunders Delhi in 1739.
The earthquake of 1755 kills up to 100,000 people in Lisbon.
The European powers fight worldwide from 1756 to 1763.
The British conquest of Bengal begins with Plassey in 1757.

The Endeavour leaves Plymouth on 26 August 1768, observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti in June 1769, charts New Zealand, lands at Botany Bay on 29 April 1770 and anchors in the Downs on 12 July 1771.

events.t: Three partitions between 1772 and 1795 end the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
James Watt's improved engine goes to work in 1776.
The Second Continental Congress adopts the Declaration at Philadelphia in 1776.
The First Fleet arrives in Australia in 1788.
The Revolution begins in Paris in 1789.
The slaves of Saint-Domingue rise in 1791; Haiti is independent in 1804.
Napoleon's first command: Montenotte in April 1796, the bridge at Lodi in May, Arcole in November, Rivoli in January 1797 and peace with Austria at Campo Formio in October.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: The expedition sails in May 1798, wins at the Pyramids on 21 July and takes Cairo, but Nelson destroys the fleet at the Nile on 3 August; Napoleon leaves Egypt for Paris on 23 August 1799.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Napoleon overthrows the Directory on 9–10 November 1799 and crowns himself emperor on 2 December 1804.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Nelson destroys the French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar on 21 October 1805.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Napoleon defeats the Russian and Austrian emperors at Austerlitz on 2 December 1805.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Prussia is crushed at Jena and Auerstedt on 14 October 1806; the Treaty of Tilsit with Russia follows on 25 June 1807.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Smolensk falls on 4–6 August 1812, Borodino is fought on 7 September and Napoleon enters an abandoned, burning Moscow on 14 September; the retreat begins on 19 October, the Berezina is crossed in November and the army is out of Russia by December.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: The allies defeat Napoleon at Leipzig on 16–19 October 1813; he abdicates on 4 April 1814 and goes to Elba.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Napoleon returns to Paris on 20 March 1815 and is beaten at Waterloo on 18 June.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of the Napoleonic era

events.t: Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 frees Gran Colombia, which breaks up in 1830.
Greece fights free of Ottoman rule between 1821 and 1830.
The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens in 1825; the first steam locomotive had run in 1804.
Officers gather their troops on Senate Square in December 1825 and are dispersed with artillery.
Telegraphy is patented in 1837; the first publicly funded line runs from Baltimore to Washington in 1844.
Britain fights the Qing over the opium trade from 1839 to 1842.
Risings sweep Europe in 1848, from Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan.
The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom is proclaimed in 1851, takes Nanjing in 1853 and is destroyed in 1864.
Britain, France and the Ottomans fight Russia from 1853 to 1856; Sevastopol is besieged.
Plague breaks out in Yunnan in 1855, reaches Hong Kong in 1894 and Bombay in 1896, and kills about 60,000 along the Chinese Eastern Railway in 1910.
Sepoys rise at Meerut and Delhi in 1857; the Company's rule ends.
Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species in 1859.
The Franco-Austrian war of 1859 opens the wars of unification; Rome is Italy's capital after 1870–1871.
Alexander II's manifesto of 1861 frees the serfs of Russia.
The Union and the Confederacy fight from 1861 to 1865.
Power returns to the emperor in 1868 and the court moves from Kyoto to Tokyo; the Boshin War of 1868–1869 ends the shogunate.
The Franco-Prussian War of 1870–1871 ends with the proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles.
The first telephone call is made in 1876 and the first exchange opens at New Haven in 1878.
Edison's practical bulb of 1879 is followed by the first large power utilities in 1882.

events.n: The Berlin Conference and the scramble for Africa
events.t: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 sets the rules of partition; by 1898 almost the whole of Africa is colonised.
The Wright brothers make the first controlled heavier-than-air flight on 17 December 1903.
Japan attacks Port Arthur on 8 February 1904 and destroys the Baltic Fleet at Tsushima; the war ends in Japanese victory in September 1905.
Troops fire on marchers approaching the Winter Palace on 22 January 1905; strikes force the October Manifesto.
Gavrilo Princip shoots Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914.
Trench lines run from the Channel to Switzerland after the Marne in September 1914; Verdun and the Somme in 1916 cost over a million casualties; the armistice is signed on 11 November 1918.
The February rising ends the monarchy on 8 March 1917; Lenin returns by train through Germany and Sweden in April; the Bolsheviks take the Winter Palace on 7 November.
Soviet Russia leaves the war at Brest-Litovsk in March 1918.
The pandemic begins in March 1918 and lasts until April 1920.
The treaty of 28 June 1919 redraws the borders of Europe.
The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics is created on 30 December 1922.
Alexander Fleming rediscovers penicillin on 3 September 1928.
The crash of 24–29 October 1929 opens the Great Depression.
Adolf Hitler is appointed chancellor of Germany on 30 January 1933.
The war begins with the coup of July 1936 and ends in Franco's victory in 1939.
Germany invades Poland on 1 September 1939; Britain and France declare war on 3 September.
Germany invades the Soviet Union in June 1941 and by December stands before Moscow and Leningrad.
Japan attacks Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 and the United States enters the war.
The battle begins in August 1942 and ends on 2 February 1943 with the German surrender.
Allied forces land in Normandy on 6 June 1944 and break out towards Paris.
Atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and Nagasaki on 9 August.
The UN Charter is signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
India and Pakistan become independent on 14–15 August 1947; partition sets millions moving across the new borders.
Israel is proclaimed on 14 May 1948.
Mao proclaims the People's Republic from Tiananmen on 1 October 1949.
The North Atlantic Treaty is signed on 4 April 1949.
North Korea invades the South on 25 June 1950.
Six states sign the Treaty of Rome on 25 March 1957, the seed of the European Union.
Sputnik 1 is launched on 4 October 1957; the space age begins.
Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space on 12 April 1961.
Construction of the Wall begins on 13 August 1961; it falls on 9 November 1989.
The crisis of 16–29 October 1962 brings the superpowers to the edge of nuclear war.
The reforms of 1968 are crushed by Warsaw Pact troops in August.
Men land on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
Saigon falls on 30 April 1975 and the Vietnam War ends.
The Shah is overthrown; the revolution is complete on 11 February 1979.
Soviet forces enter Afghanistan on 24 December 1979.
Reactor 4 explodes on 26 April 1986.
The protests of April–June 1989 end in massacre on 4 June.
Poland votes on 4 June 1989, the Berlin Wall falls on 9 November, the Velvet Revolution begins in Prague on 24 November and Ceaușescu is executed on 25 December.
Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first website at CERN on 20 December 1990.
Germany is reunited on 3 October 1990.

events.n: The dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.t: The Belovezha Accords dissolve the Union; the Supreme Soviet confirms it on 26 December 1991 and fifteen republics are independent.
The Ten-Day War in Slovenia in June 1991 opens the wars; Kosovo ends them in June 1999.
Signed on 7 February 1992 and in force from 1 November 1993, the treaty creates the European Union.
The shooting down of the presidents' aircraft on 6 April 1994 triggers the genocide.
Apartheid ends and Nelson Mandela is inaugurated on 10 May 1994.
Hong Kong passes from Britain to China on 1 July 1997.
The euro is introduced to the markets on 1 January 1999 and enters circulation on 1 January 2002.
About 2,977 people die in the attacks on the United States on 11 September 2001; the invasion of Afghanistan follows on 7 October.
The United States invades Iraq on 19 March 2003.
The earthquake and tsunami of 26 December 2004 kill about 230,000 people.
Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008.
Risings begin in Tunisia in 2010 and spread in 2011 to Egypt, Libya, Yemen, Bahrain and Syria.
The earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 cause the meltdown at Fukushima.
After Yanukovych's fall in February 2014 Russia annexes Crimea and war begins in the Donbas.
195 nations agree to cut emissions in December 2015.
Britain votes to leave the European Union on 23 June 2016.
The virus spreads from China late in 2019 and across the world in 2020, with at least 1.8 million deaths in the first year.
Russia invades Ukraine on 24 February 2022, escalating the war begun in 2014.
Hamas attacks Israel on 7 October 2023 and the Gaza war begins.
